glosses: Censure.

examples.text: Blame came from all directions.

glosses: Culpability for something negative or undesirable.

examples.text: The blame for starting the fire lies with the arsonist.

glosses: Responsibility for something meriting censure.

examples.text: They accepted the blame, but it was an accident.

glosses: A source control feature that can show which user was responsible for a particular portion of the source code.
To assert or consider that someone is the cause of something negative; to place blame; to attribute responsibility (for something negative or for doing something negative).

examples.text: The student driver was blamed for the accident.
After what happened at the wedding, I wouldn't blame you if you never spoke to them again.
These peculiarities of Dorothea's character caused Mr Brooke to be all the more blamed in neighbouring families for not securing some middle-aged lady as guide and companion to his nieces.
That was the year that Sir Richard was writing his volume on Domestic Life in Tartary. The critics all blamed it for a lack of concentration.

glosses: To assert the cause of some bad event.

examples.text: We blamed the accident on the student driver.

examples.text: Sur Twitter, le professeur en médecine interne Josh Barocas, dans le Colorado, a critiqué l’attitude dangereuse du chef d’État, qu’il a même qualifiée de « préjudiciable ».

examples.text: Critiquer un ouvrage, un écrivain. - Il critique les actions, la conduite de tout le monde.
